> 天下莫柔弱於水，而攻堅強者莫之能勝，以其無以易之.

Chapter 77 was the bow being strung. Chapter 78 is water — and four characters in it repay a second look.

## 易 pictures water poured from one vessel to another

說文 gives 易 as 蜥蜴 — a lizard. That is one account. But in the older forms there is another: two vessels facing each other, water going from one into the other.

And that is exactly 易's sense of transfer, of substitution: what is here is poured over there.

So 以其無以易之 means: there is nothing that can be poured out of it, nothing that can take its place. No one can substitute for it.

The vessels can be changed. The water is not poured off.

## 垢 is mud, from 土

垢: 濁也, from 土. Dirt is earth.

And what does water do when it takes on earth? The earth goes down, and the water is clear again.

澄: 清也.

So 受垢 has three steps: receive, settle, clear.

The water does not eat the dirt. It puts it down.

## 社 is the god of the ground

社: 地主也, from 示 and 土 — the spirit of the soil.

垢 is from 土; 社 is from 土.

So 受國之垢，是謂社稷主 — the one who has taken the country's mud is the one fit to be the master of its soil. Same material, and only the one who has held it can stand over it.

## 弱之勝強，柔之勝剛，天下莫不知，莫能行

Everyone knows it; no one can do it.

This is the most honest sentence in the book about its own reception. The principle is not obscure — it is universally acknowledged and universally unimplemented, and the gap is not informational.

Which means the chapter is not teaching a fact. It is describing a capacity.

## 正言若反

Straight words look reversed.

反, as in chapter 25's 反者道之動, is the counter-motion. What is said straight sounds backwards — not because it is paradoxical, but because the direction of the saying runs against the direction of ordinary valuation.

## Why this follows 77

77: the surplus is visible and the short is not, so the human way flows toward the visible.
78: water flows the other way, into the low place, and takes the dirt there.

Two flows, opposite directions, and the chapter's claim is that the second is stronger — not morally, but because it has nothing to defend.

## A test

Take the criticism you have been avoiding — the thing about your work that someone has said and you have not let settle. The chapter's instruction is not to accept it. It is to let it go down and see whether the water clears.
